tiers.corp: Public company, corporate investor, or venture-backed
tiers.indie: Independent (owner-operated, no outside institutional owner found)

places.name: Levain Bakery
places.owner: Founders Pam Weekes & Connie McDonald, with growth-equity firm Stripes
places.note: Deal databases record a 2018 investment by New York growth-equity firm Stripes that funded Levain's expansion beyond its Upper West Side original; the founders remain co-owners. The stake size isn't public. The Williamsburg shop opened July 2020.

sources.label: Brooklyn Paper: Levain opens in Williamsburg

places.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
places.owner: Centurium Capital (private equity; also the largest shareholder of Luckin Coffee)
places.note: Nestlé bought a majority stake in 2017 and sold the business to Chinese private-equity firm Centurium Capital in April 2026.

sources.label: Daily Coffee News: Nestlé confirms sale to Centurium (Apr 2026)

places.name: Van Leeuwen Ice Cream
places.owner: Founders Ben & Pete Van Leeuwen and Laura O'Neill, with minority investors Strand Equity and NextWorld Evergreen
places.note: This is a Brooklyn-born brand that took institutional money: a 2018 minority investment led by growth-equity firm Strand Equity, then an $18.7M Series B led by NextWorld Evergreen in 2020.

sources.label: Business Wire: NextWorld leads Series B (2020)

places.name: Sweet Chick
places.owner: Founders Table Restaurant Group, which is financed by L Catterton
places.note: The Williamsburg original, opened in 2012. In 2022 it took Series A money from Founders Table, the Chopt/Dos Toros holding company that private-equity firm L Catterton financed.

sources.label: PR Newswire: Sweet Chick partners with Founders Table (2022)
NRN: Founders Table deal financed by L Catterton
DNAinfo: Sweet Chick opens on Bedford

places.name: Dos Toros Taqueria
places.owner: Founders Table Restaurant Group (Chopt's parent), financed by L Catterton
places.note: Chopt bought Dos Toros in 2020 and formed the Founders Table holding company. NRN reported the deal as "financed by private equity firm L Catterton."

sources.label: NRN: Chopt buys Dos Toros, financed by L Catterton (Jan 2020)

places.name: Blank Street
places.owner: Venture-backed (General Catalyst and Tiger Global led its $25M Series A)
chain: Venture capital: General Catalyst, Tiger Global and others
places.note: Blank Street started as a cart in Williamsburg in 2020 and opened its first brick-and-mortar shop here by the Bedford Ave L. VC money then scaled it across NYC, London and beyond.

sources.label: TechCrunch: General Catalyst & Tiger Global lead $25M

places.name: Sweetgreen
places.owner: Sweetgreen, Inc. (NYSE: SG)
places.note: Sweetgreen was VC-funded before its 2021 IPO and is now publicly traded. This store opened across from Whole Foods in 2014.

places.name: Shake Shack
places.owner: Shake Shack Inc. (NYSE: SHAK)
places.note: Publicly traded since 2015. The Williamsburg Shack opened in 2018 in Blue Bottle's old Berry St space.

sources.label: UrbanDaddy: Shake Shack lands in Williamsburg

places.name: CAVA
places.owner: CAVA Group, Inc. (NYSE: CAVA)
places.note: This Mediterranean chain went public in 2023 after years of private-equity and venture funding.

places.name: Peter Luger Steak House
places.owner: The Forman and Sloyer families (Amy Rubenstein, Marilyn Spiera)
places.note: Open since 1887 under the Williamsburg Bridge. Ownership passed to the families of Sol Forman and Seymour Sloyer in 2001.

places.name: Bamonte's
places.owner: Anthony Bamonte and his daughters
places.note: Red-sauce Italian, run by the same family for four generations. Pasquale Bamonte opened it as Liberty Hall in 1900.

places.name: Lilia
places.owner: Chef Missy Robbins and partner Sean Feeney
places.note: Chef-owned pasta destination in a former auto-body shop. We found no outside institutional investor in public reporting.

places.name: Misi
places.owner: Chef Missy Robbins and partner Sean Feeney
places.note: Lilia's sibling, on the ground floor of the Domino Sugar site. The building is big-developer real estate, but the restaurant is chef-owned.

places.name: Fini Pizza
places.owner: Sean Feeney (Lilia / Misi partner)
places.note: A slice shop from the Lilia/Misi partner. It is now multi-unit, but we found no outside institutional owner.

sources.label: Yahoo/Food & Wine: Sean Feeney opens Fini

places.name: L'Industrie Pizzeria
places.owner: Massimo Laveglia
places.note: This is the 2017 flagship. Later Manhattan shops brought in the Saper brothers (ex-Eataly) as operating partners, which isn't institutional capital.

places.name: Diner
places.owner: Andrew Tarlow
places.note: A 1920s dining car that kicked off the Williamsburg restaurant boom in 1998. It anchors Tarlow's independent group, which also runs St. Anselm and the Wythe Hotel's restaurants.

sources.label: Resy: How Andrew Tarlow built his Brooklyn empire

places.name: St. Anselm
places.owner: Andrew Tarlow
places.note: A no-reservations grill from the Diner team.

places.name: Maison Premiere
places.owner: Joshua Boissy & Krystof Zizka
places.note: Oyster and absinthe bar opened in 2011, still run by its two founders.

places.name: The Four Horsemen
places.owner: James Murphy, Christina Topsøe and partners
places.note: Natural-wine bar opened in 2015 by LCD Soundsystem's James Murphy and friends.

sources.label: BrooklynVegan: James Murphy opening a wine bar

places.name: Aska
places.owner: Chef Fredrik Berselius
places.note: Two-Michelin-star Scandinavian tasting menu in an 1860s warehouse by the bridge.

sources.label: Brooklyn Magazine: Aska rises from the ashes

places.name: Pies 'n' Thighs
places.owner: Sarah Sanneh & Carolyn Bane
places.note: Fried chicken and pie, run by its two founders since the 2000s.

sources.label: Total Food Service: the duo persists

places.name: Sunday in Brooklyn
places.owner: Founding partners Jaime Young, Adam Landsman & Todd Enany
places.note: Brunch institution and pantry on Wythe. We found no institutional investor.

places.name: Devoción
places.owner: Founder Steven Sutton
places.note: Colombian farm-to-cup roaster in a skylit warehouse. We found no outside institutional owner.

sources.label: Daily Coffee News: Devoción opens in Williamsburg

places.name: Shalom Japan
places.owner: Chefs Aaron Israel & Sawako Okochi
places.note: Jewish-Japanese cooking from the husband-and-wife chef team.

places.name: Kellogg's Diner
places.owner: Restaurateur Louis Skibar (Coppelia, Toloache)
places.note: The 1928 diner went bankrupt in 2023 and reopened in 2024 under a local restaurateur, not a chain or fund.

sources.label: Time Out: first look at the reopened Kellogg's

places.name: Win Son
places.owner: Josh Ku & Trigg Brown
places.note: Taiwanese-American restaurant with a bakery across the street.

places.name: Bonnie's
places.owner: Chef Calvin Eng
places.note: Cantonese-American restaurant from a Win Son alum, named for his mother.

places.name: Laser Wolf
places.owner: CookNSolo (Michael Solomonov & Steven Cook), an independent Philadelphia group
chain: Host building: The Hoxton, an Ennismore/Accor brand
places.note: Mixed case: the restaurant operator is independent, but it rents its rooftop from The Hoxton, part of Accor's Ennismore lifestyle-hotel group.

sources.label: Skift: Accor and Ennismore close merger

places.name: Westlight
places.owner: NoHo Hospitality Group (Andrew Carmellini, Luke Ostrom, Josh Pickard)
places.note: Rooftop bar run by a privately held NYC restaurant group. We found no PE owner, but the group is not a single-site independent.

places.name: PopUp Bagels
places.owner: Growth-equity firm Stripes (majority), with Tiger Global as an investor
places.note: This feels like a viral bagel pop-up, but Stripes led its 2024 Series A and took a majority stake in 2025. Hedge fund Tiger Global then invested at a valuation of about $300M in spring 2026. The Williamsburg shop opened in April 2025.

sources.label: Hedgeweek: Tiger Global invests at $300M valuation (Apr 2026)

places.name: Black Seed Bagels
places.owner: Private-equity firm Valor Equity Partners (portfolio company)
places.note: Black Seed began as a Nolita bagel shop and grew to about 10 NYC stores. Chicago-based Valor Equity Partners lists it as a portfolio company. The size of the stake isn't public.

sources.label: Valor Equity Partners: Black Seed company profile
Brownstoner: Black Seed comes to 214 Berry St

places.name: Emmy Squared Pizza
places.owner: Founders Emily & Matt Hyland and CEO Howard Greenstone, plus two private-equity firms (unnamed)
places.note: The Detroit-style pizza chain opened its second shop here in 2016. Commercial Observer reported that two private-equity firms bought shares from earlier investors in 2022. The firms and price weren't disclosed.

sources.label: Commercial Observer: How Emmy Squared went from Brooklyn to the world (2023)

places.name: Brooklyn Brewery
places.owner: Founders and management, with Japan's Kirin holding about 24.6%
places.note: Williamsburg's signature brewery sold close to a quarter of itself to Japanese brewing giant Kirin in 2016 to fund global growth. It's still majority-owned by its founders and management.

sources.label: Kirin Holdings: capital partnership with Brooklyn Brewery (2016)

places.name: Roberta's
places.owner: Founding partners, with Chorus Hospitality (billionaire Michael Tisch's investment vehicle)
places.note: The scrappy East Williamsburg/Bushwick pizzeria that defined Brooklyn cool sold a stake to Chorus Hospitality, backed by Loews heir Michael Tisch, in 2016. That money helped fund its frozen pizza line and expansion. The stake size wasn't disclosed.

sources.label: Forward: Michael Tisch gets a slice of Roberta's
Bushwick Daily: Roberta's and the billionaires

places.name: Bakeri
places.owner: Founder Nina Brondmo
places.note: Norwegian-style bakery opened in 2009 by Nina Brondmo. It has three small shops and no outside investor that we could find.

sources.label: amNY: Bakeri and Brooklyn's family-run bakeries

places.name: Café Mogador
places.owner: The founding family (Mogador has been family-run since 1983)
places.note: The East Village Moroccan institution's Williamsburg outpost. The restaurant says the same family still owns and runs both locations.

sources.label: Brooklyn Magazine: Mogador comes to Williamsburg
